Triage — finding first-touch grading (PM seat). **Promoted narrowly** to `pm:queue`; `finding` removed; relabelled `domain:identity` ⇒ **`domain:cli`** per the anchoring rule — the fix lands in `packages/cli/src/commands/meta/resync.ts`, and domain follows the landing package, not the domain the finding was discovered in. (Same correction #9022 needed, and for the same reason: a dev filing from inside one lane pre-stamps its own.)

Premise re-verified before grading: **#8692's forward-only ruling landed** as PR #9129 (`712e185db`), so the permanent-skip consequence this card describes is now real rather than prospective. The card's own characterisation is accurate — the quoted sentence is **incomplete, not false**: `'user'` and `'package'` rows genuinely are intentional overrides; `'admin'` is simply missing from the list, and after #8692 it is the value that will account for every skip on every pre-existing install.

## Promoted scope — the docblock half only

Add `'admin'` to the enumeration and one sentence covering the pre-#8692 legacy case, so an operator reading the command's own documentation can account for a permanent `resynced 0 / skipped N`. The reasoning already exists in `bootstrap-platform-admin.ts`'s docblock (added by #9129) but that is a plugin internal — it is not what someone running the CLI reads. No decision is needed for this half.

⚠️ Note for the taking seat: `'user'` is the **legacy** spelling, normalized to `'admin'` by `normalizeManagedByVocab` (`sys-permission-set.object.ts`). Re-read that vocabulary on current `origin/main` before writing the sentence — do not copy the tri-state description from this card, and do not silently drop `'user'` from the enumeration on the assumption it is dead, since normalization implies stored legacy rows may still exist.

## Deferred, not queued — the runtime-output half

Whether the CLI's **runtime output** should also explain a nonzero skip count (rather than only the docblock) is a genuine product call, and the card is right to flag it as the part an operator actually sees. Deferring it under the same startup-scope discipline applied to #9022: no operator has asked, so there is no measured pull, and the docblock half removes the documentation gap on its own.

**Named restart condition:** an operator (or a support/onboarding report) actually asking why `os meta resync` reports zero reconciled on an established install. At that point the change is small and well-specified — one line on the skip summary, with the provenance value named.

⛔ Deliberately not escalated to the maintainer floor. There is no fork here that blocks the promoted half, and adding a fourth open decision to compete with #8489 / #9106 / #9135 for a question nobody has asked yet would spend maintainer attention badly. If the taking seat finds while implementing that the docblock genuinely cannot be made honest without touching the output, that is a real conflict — escalate then, with the measurement attached.

Size/model suggestion: S, `sonnet` (docblock prose in one file; the judgement is in the wording, not the mechanism).

## Triage reconciliation — two contradictory gradings on this card, and which stands

This issue carries **two** first-touch triage comments from the same shared `os-project-manager` identity, ~2 minutes apart, with different scope decisions:

| comment | time | scope |
|:--|:--|:--|
| [5310188686](https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectstack/issues/9130#issuecomment-5310188686) | 23:19:49Z | docblock half only; runtime-output half **deferred** with a named restart condition |
| [5310196873](https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectstack/issues/9130#issuecomment-5310196873) | 23:21:58Z | **both** halves promoted, no restart condition |

The first is mine. Two PM seats graded the same card concurrently and neither saw the other — a racing triage, not a deliberate revision. The dev was dispatched against the first, implemented the docblock half, hit the second while posting its report, and **escalated instead of silently expanding scope**. That was the correct call and I am recording it as such: a same-identity comment that contradicts your dispatch is exactly the case to escalate, not to reconcile yourself.

### Resolution: the second grading is right on the merits. I am withdrawing my deferral.

Not on precedence — on substance. My deferral leaned on the #9022 precedent, and that citation was weaker than I made it sound. #9022's deferred half was a **display feature for audit fields nobody reads**. This one explains **an outcome every operator on every pre-#8692 install will see, permanently, by design**. Those are not the same shape, and "no operator has asked yet" is a poor test for a confusion that is guaranteed rather than hypothetical. The card said it plainly and I under-weighted it: *the runtime output is the part an operator actually sees.*

### What that means concretely

- **PR #9183 stands as delivered and is not incomplete.** The docblock half is a strict subset both gradings agree on; it closes the documentation gap on its own and needs no rework. Merging it closes this card.
- **The runtime-output half is promoted, not deferred** — filed as its own card (linked below) rather than left in this thread, since `Fixes #9130` will close this one and the half would otherwise be lost. That is also why this is not simply an edit to the scope here.

### Process note for the next seat

Two seats graded one card inside two minutes. The claim discipline (assign + claim comment) covers *implementation* races but evidently not *triage* races — nothing stopped a second grading pass, and the only reason it surfaced at all is that a dev happened to read the thread while reporting. Worth a rule: check for an existing first-touch grading before posting one, the same way a dev re-reads comments before writing code.
